/-!
# Conjecture 9.77

by V. P. Shunkov

Does there exist an infinite finitely generated residually finite binary finite
group all of whose Sylow subgroups are finite?

A. V. Rozhkov (Dr. of Sci. Disser., 1997) showed that such a group does exist
if the condition of finiteness of the Sylow subgroups is weakened to local
finiteness.

Here a group is *residually finite* if every non-trivial element survives in some
finite quotient, *binary finite* if every subgroup generated by two elements is
finite, and *locally finite* if every finitely generated subgroup is finite.
A *Sylow $p$-subgroup* of an arbitrary (possibly infinite) group is a maximal
$p$-subgroup, as in Mathlib's `Sylow p G`.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

blocks.code:
def IsResiduallyFinite : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 → ∃ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal ∧ N.FiniteIndex ∧ g ∉ N
blocks.docstring:
A group $G$ is *residually finite* if for every non-trivial element $g \in G$
there is a normal subgroup $N$ of finite index in $G$ with $g \notin N$, i.e. $g$ has
non-trivial image in the finite quotient $G / N$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Nothing in Mathlib (only a docstring mention in GroupTheory/Torsion.lean); `Subgroup.Normal` and `Subgroup.FiniteIndex` are used as building blocks.
justification.name: Kourovka.«9.77».IsResiduallyFinite
justification.why_needed: Residual finiteness of a group has no definition in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib. Defined as: every g ≠ 1 lies outside some normal subgroup of finite index (equivalently, has non-trivial image in some finite quotient).

blocks.name: IsResiduallyFinite
blocks.text:
/-- A group $G$ is *residually finite* if for every non-trivial element $g \in G$
there is a normal subgroup $N$ of finite index in $G$ with $g \notin N$, i.e. $g$ has
non-trivial image in the finite quotient $G / N$. -/
def IsResiduallyFinite : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 → ∃ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal ∧ N.FiniteIndex ∧ g ∉ N

blocks.code:
def IsBinaryFinite : Prop :=
  ∀ x y : G, Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y})
blocks.docstring:
A group $G$ is *binary finite* if every subgroup generated by two elements is
finite.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `Monoid.IsTorsion` (strictly weaker: only 1-generated subgroups finite); `Subgroup.FG` (used for local finiteness instead).
justification.name: Kourovka.«9.77».IsBinaryFinite
justification.why_needed: 'Binary finite' (every 2-generated subgroup is finite, Shunkov's terminology) has no Mathlib counterpart. Defined as `∀ x y : G, Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y})`.

def IsLocallyFinite : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Finite H
blocks.docstring: A group $G$ is *locally finite* if every finitely generated subgroup is finite.

justification.name: Kourovka.«9.77».IsLocallyFinite
justification.why_needed: Local finiteness of a group (every finitely generated subgroup is finite) has no Mathlib definition (only `LocallyFiniteOrder`, unrelated). Defined as `∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Finite H`; applied to the coerced type `↥P` of a Sylow subgroup.

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsBinaryFinite.isTorsion (h : IsBinaryFinite G) : Monoid.IsTorsion G := by
  intro g
  have := h g g
  have hg : g ∈ Subgroup.closure ({g, g} : Set G) := Subgroup.subset_closure (by simp)
  have hpos := orderOf_pos (⟨g, hg⟩ : Subgroup.closure ({g, g} : Set G))
  rw [Subgroup.orderOf_mk] at hpos
  exact orderOf_pos_iff.mp hpos

claims.decomposer_note: Yes/no existence question: 'binary finite' means every 2-generated subgroup is finite (hence the group is periodic); 'all Sylow subgroups finite' means for every prime p every Sylow p-subgroup, i.e. every maximal p-subgroup in the sense of Mathlib's `Sylow p G` (valid for infinite groups), is finite — equivalently every p-subgroup is finite; residual finiteness (every nontrivial element survives in some finite quotient) has no Mathlib definition and must be defined locally; the existence must be stated with ∃ ... ∧ (not →) and the group must be explicitly Infinite and finitely generated.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same faithful proposition: `answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), Infinite G ∧ Group.FG G ∧ IsResiduallyFinite G ∧ IsBinaryFinite G ∧ ∀ p, p.Prime → ∀ P : Sylow p G, Finite P`. Checks: existence uses ∧ (not →); G is explicitly Infinite and finitely generated; 'binary finite' = every 2-generated subgroup `Subgroup.closure {x, y}` is finite (x = y allowed, so periodicity follows, proved as API lemma); Sylow subgroups are Mathlib's `Sylow p G` = maximal p-subgroups (valid for infinite groups, nonempty by Zorn, so never vacuous) restricted to primes p (necessary: `IsPGroup 0` holds for every group, so `Sylow 0 G = ⊤` would wrongly force G finite); `Finite P` elaborates to `Finite ↥P` (verified); residual finiteness defined locally via finite-index normal subgroups, classically equivalent to the homomorphism form used by c02/c04/c07/c08. Quantifying G over `Type` is harmless since finitely generated groups are countable. c03 chosen for its named, documented bespoke definitions plus proved API/test lemmas (finite ⇒ all three properties; locally finite ⇒ binary finite ⇒ torsion; ℤ is not binary finite), matching CONTRIBUTING's request for basic API tests of bespoke definitions.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 9.77

by V. P. Shunkov

Does there exist an infinite finitely generated residually finite binary finite
group all of whose Sylow subgroups are finite?

A. V. Rozhkov (Dr. of Sci. Disser., 1997) showed that such a group does exist
if the condition of finiteness of the Sylow subgroups is weakened to local
finiteness.

Here a group is *residually finite* if every non-trivial element survives in some
finite quotient, *binary finite* if every subgroup generated by two elements is
finite, and *locally finite* if every finitely generated subgroup is finite.
A *Sylow $p$-subgroup* of an arbitrary (possibly infinite) group is a maximal
$p$-subgroup, as in Mathlib's `Sylow p G`.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«9.77»

variable (G : Type*) [Group G]

/-- A group $G$ is *residually finite* if for every non-trivial element $g \in G$
there is a normal subgroup $N$ of finite index in $G$ with $g \notin N$, i.e. $g$ has
non-trivial image in the finite quotient $G / N$. -/
def IsResiduallyFinite : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 → ∃ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal ∧ N.FiniteIndex ∧ g ∉ N

/-- A group $G$ is *binary finite* if every subgroup generated by two elements is
finite. -/
def IsBinaryFinite : Prop :=
  ∀ x y : G, Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y})

/-- A group $G$ is *locally finite* if every finitely generated subgroup is finite. -/
def IsLocallyFinite : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Finite H

variable {G}

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsResiduallyFinite.of_finite [Finite G] : IsResiduallyFinite G :=
  fun g hg => ⟨⊥, inferInstance, inferInstance, by simpa using hg⟩

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsBinaryFinite.of_finite [Finite G] : IsBinaryFinite G :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstance

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsLocallyFinite.of_finite [Finite G] : IsLocallyFinite G :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstance

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsLocallyFinite.isBinaryFinite (h : IsLocallyFinite G) : IsBinaryFinite G :=
  fun x y => h _ <| (Subgroup.fg_iff _).mpr ⟨{x, y}, rfl, Set.toFinite _⟩

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsBinaryFinite.isTorsion (h : IsBinaryFinite G) : Monoid.IsTorsion G := by
  intro g
  have := h g g
  have hg : g ∈ Subgroup.closure ({g, g} : Set G) := Subgroup.subset_closure (by simp)
  have hpos := orderOf_pos (⟨g, hg⟩ : Subgroup.closure ({g, g} : Set G))
  rw [Subgroup.orderOf_mk] at hpos
  exact orderOf_pos_iff.mp hpos

/-- Test that the integers are not binary finite. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem not_isBinaryFinite_int : ¬ IsBinaryFinite (Multiplicative ℤ) := by
  intro h
  have := h.isTorsion (Multiplicative.ofAdd 1)
  simp [isOfFinOrder_iff_pow_eq_one] at this

/--
Does there exist an infinite finitely generated residually finite binary finite
group all of whose Sylow subgroups are finite?

Here "all Sylow subgroups are finite" means that for every prime $p$, every Sylow
$p$-subgroup (maximal $p$-subgroup) of $G$ is finite.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.77» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), Infinite G ∧ Group.FG G ∧ IsResiduallyFinite G ∧
      IsBinaryFinite G ∧ ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → ∀ P : Sylow p G, Finite P := by
  sorry

/--
A. V. Rozhkov (Dr. of Sci. Disser., 1997) showed that there exists an infinite
finitely generated residually finite binary finite group all of whose Sylow
subgroups are locally finite, i.e. for every prime $p$ every Sylow $p$-subgroup
(maximal $p$-subgroup) of $G$ is a locally finite group.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.77».variants.locally_finite_sylow :
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), Infinite G ∧ Group.FG G ∧ IsResiduallyFinite G ∧
      IsBinaryFinite G ∧ ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → ∀ P : Sylow p G, IsLocallyFinite P := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.77»

items: 'Sylow subgroup' is taken in the sense of Mathlib's `Sylow p G`, i.e. a maximal p-subgroup; this matches the standard meaning for infinite groups (and Shunkov's school), and `Sylow.nonempty` guarantees such subgroups exist, so the finiteness condition is never vacuous. Since every p-subgroup lies in a Sylow p-subgroup (`IsPGroup.exists_le_sylow`), 'all Sylow p-subgroups finite' is equivalent to 'all p-subgroups finite'.

p is restricted to primes via `p.Prime →` (rather than `[Fact p.Prime]`), following the wording 'Sylow subgroups'. For composite p Mathlib's `Sylow p G` would add nothing new (a `Sylow 4 G` is a `Sylow 2 G`, and `Sylow 0/1 G` is trivial), but the prime restriction is the faithful reading.
Residual finiteness is defined via normal subgroups of finite index (`N.Normal ∧ N.FiniteIndex ∧ g ∉ N`) rather than via homomorphisms onto finite groups; the two are equivalent.

Binary finiteness uses `Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y})` (finiteness of the subgroup as a type); x = y is allowed, so the definition implies periodicity (proved as API lemma `IsBinaryFinite.isTorsion`).

Local finiteness of a Sylow subgroup P is expressed as `IsLocallyFinite ↥P`, i.e. every finitely generated subgroup of P (as a group in its own right) is finite; this equals 'every finitely generated subgroup of G contained in P is finite'.
The group is quantified over `Type` (universe 0), consistent with other Kourovka files (1_74, 1_40); existence is stated with `∃ ... ∧` and the group is explicitly `Infinite` and `Group.FG`.

The variant is tagged `research solved` with no `formal_proof` attribute, since Rozhkov's 1997 dissertation is an informal result; a few small proven `API`/`test` lemmas sanity-check the bespoke definitions (finite groups satisfy all three; locally finite ⇒ binary finite ⇒ torsion; ℤ is not binary finite).

reviewer_notes: No candidate omitted a slot and none raised decomposition objections; all eight compiled and agree on the mathematical content, differing only in cosmetic choices (hom-based vs. finite-index-normal-subgroup residual finiteness; inline vs. named binary-finite predicate; presence of API lemmas). Interpretive choices a reviewer should be aware of: (1) 'Sylow subgroup' of an infinite group is taken as a maximal p-subgroup (Mathlib `Sylow p G`), the standard meaning in Shunkov's school; since every p-subgroup lies in a Sylow p-subgroup this is equivalent to 'every p-subgroup is finite'. (2) 'binary finite' = every two elements generate a finite subgroup. (3) The variant is tagged `research solved` on the strength of the notebook's own assertion about Rozhkov's dissertation. The final file is c03 verbatim; it compiles with only the two expected `declaration uses 'sorry'` warnings. A reviewer may prefer moving `IsResiduallyFinite`/`IsLocallyFinite` to FormalConjecturesForMathlib as generic definitions; they are kept in the problem file here because the pipeline produces a single file.
